result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers explain well why errors during typing are premature and irritating, both clear errors live once the value is valid, and both apply the advice carefully to email, password (a live checklist as the exception) and promo code. B follows the rubric's blur-or-submit timing more literally and adds API-cost and ARIA tips. A argues for submit-first with a well-reasoned warning about blur, and adds concrete autocomplete, error-summary and server-side details, so overall they come out about equal. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers explain why errors that appear mid-typing are premature and irritating, both recommend live re-checking that clears the error once the value is valid, and both treat the password checklist as live guidance rather than an error. A builds on the 'reward early, punish late' blur pattern and adds a good point about promo lookups overloading the API. B defaults to validating on submit, warns that blur can fire at odd moments, and adds more field-specific detail (autocomplete attributes, allowing paste, server-side checks, keeping input). Their strengths offset each other, so neither is clearly better.
